Option 1) + and ÷

The given equation is, 2 + 5 - 3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 14.

Interchanging the signs, we get,

LHS = 2 ÷ 5 - 3 × 6 + 2 

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by ÷ is calculated first.

LHS = 0.4 - 3 × 6 + 2 

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by × is calculated next.

LHS = 0.4 - 18 + 2 

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by + is calculated next.

LHS = 0.4 - 20

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by - is calculated next.

LHS = -19.6 which is not equal to RHS.

Thus, option 1 is incorrect.

Option 2) × and ÷

The given equation is, 2 + 5 - 3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 14.

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by ÷ is calculated first.

LHS = 2 + 5 - 0.5 × 2

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by × is calculated next.

LHS = 2 + 5 - 1

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by + is calculated next.

LHS = 7 - 1 = 6 which is not equal to RHS.

Thus, option 2 is incorrect.

Option 3) - and ×

The given equation is, 2 + 5 - 3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 14.

Interchanging the signs, we get,

LHS = 2 + 5 × 3 - 6 ÷ 2

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by ÷ is calculated first.

LHS = 2 + 5 × 3 - 3

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by × is calculated next.

LHS = 2 + 15 - 3

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by + is calculated next.

LHS = 17 - 3 = 14 = RHS.

Thus, option 3 is correct.

By the BODMAS rule, the terms related by × is calculated next.

LHS = 10 - 3 + 3

questions.question: What is the greatest number of 4-digits which is divisible by 45, 25 and 5?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of 45, 25, and 5: **LCM = 225**.

The **greatest 4-digit number** is 9999.

Divide 9999 by 225 to find the remainder: 9999 ÷ 225 → **Remainder = 99**.

Subtract the remainder from 9999: 9999 − 99 = 9900.

**∴ The correct answer is 9900.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 45, 25, and 5.

Target: Greatest 4-digit number.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = (Greatest 4-digit number) − (Remainder when Greatest 4-digit number is divided by LCM of divisors).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f494528228b5dfc1adbe47f63cae4649188615949602ae8d818289da06439c28.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 45 = 3² × 5¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 25 = 5²

⇒ Prime factorization of 5 = 5¹

⇒ **LCM** = 3² × 5² = 9 × 25 = 225

⇒ Greatest 4-digit number = 9999

⇒ Divide 9999 by 225: 9999 = (225 × 44) + 99

⇒ **Required Number** = 9999 − 99 = 9900

**∴ The correct answer is 9900.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 25

A number is divisible by 25 if its last two digits are 00, 25, 50, or 75.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the given numbers. It is calculated by taking the product of the highest power of all prime factors involved.

Dividend Relation

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. To find a perfectly divisible number, subtract the remainder from the dividend.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about Nagara or North Indian Temple Style Architecture?

options.text: There were no tower or shikhara.
There was no Kalasha, the topmost part of the temple.
The garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nagara or North Indian Temple Style:

 
 
• Nagara (in North India) is associated with the land between the Himalayas and Vindhyas.
 
• The Nagara style is associated with the land between the Himalayas and Vindhyas, the Dravida style with the land between the Krishna and Kaveri rivers, while the Vesara style is sometimes associated with the area between the Vindhyas and the Krishna river.
 
• In North India, it is common for an entire temple to be built on a stone platform with steps leading up to it.
 
• It does not usually have elaborate boundary walls or gateways.
 
• While the earliest temples had just one tower or shikhara, later temples had several.
 
• The garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower.
 
• There are many subdivisions of nagara temples depending on the shape of the shikhara.
 
• The second major type of architectural form in the nagara order is the phamsana, which tends to be broader and shorter than the Latina ones.
 
• Their roofs are composed of several slabs that gently rise to a single point over the centre of the building, unlike the Latina ones which look like sharply rising tall towers.
 
• The third main sub-type of the nagara building is generally called the valabhi type.
 
• These are rectangular buildings with a roof that rises into a vaulted chamber.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dravida Or South Indian Temple Style

 
 
• Unlike the nagara temple, the Dravida temple is enclosed within a compound wall.
 
• The front wall has an entrance gateway in its center, which is known as a gopuram.
 
• The shape of the main temple tower known as vimana in Tamil Nadu is like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically rather than the curving shikhara of North India.
 
• It is common to find a large water reservoir, or a temple tank, enclosed within the complex.
 
• Subsidiary shrines are either incorporated within the main temple tower or located as distinct, separate small shrines beside the main temple.
 
• Kanchipuram, Thanjavur or Tanjore, Madurai, and Kumbakonam are the most famous temple towns of Tamil Nadu, where, during the 8th-12th centuries, the role of the temple was not limited to religious matters alone.
 
 
 
• The Vesara Style:-
 
 
• It is a hybrid temple architecture. It has features of both the Nagara and Dravidian style of temple architecture.
 
• In particular, the shape of the superstructure over the sanctum is usually pyramidal in profile, and shorter than the northern shikhara tower.
 
• In plan, the walls and superstructure are broadly circular, or a straight-sided cone, though its geometry is based on rotating a square imposed on a circle.
